We are discussing the October launch and the support handover.
The first proposal was to launch on 18 October 2026. The team rejected that date because billing migration is still unfinished. The final decision is a staged rollout on 25 October 2026, with 10 percent of customers on day one and all remaining customers only after the billing checks pass. A smaller rollout reduces rollback risk, but it also delays revenue. The current test budget is $500.
Ruben will send the migration checklist by Friday, 16 October. Alice will verify the billing tests by 20 October. Alice will notify customers after billing checks pass. Ruben said, "We cannot ship until billing is stable."
A participant says, "I will ask support about weekend coverage." No one identifies that participant.
For support handover, the team agreed to keep the old escalation channel open until 30 October. Alice will draft the handover guide by 22 October. The guide must explain how to roll back, and the dependency is the migration checklist. There is still an unanswered question about who will cover support during the weekend. An important constraint is that the support team has only two people on weekends. Keeping the old channel creates some duplicate work, but the team preferred that to losing urgent customer messages. Alice said, "We need a named backup before the first customer moves."

Back to launch planning: the team revised the test budget from $500 to $650 because an extra billing scenario needs coverage. That change replaces the earlier $500 budget. They discussed an alternative of launching everyone at once, but rejected it because rollback would affect all customers. The launch date remains 25 October 2026. Ruben will book the rollout review for 23 October. The unresolved launch question is whether the extra scenario can be tested without another staging environment. The team wants the review to use the actual billing test results rather than a slide deck.
